title: Jeremiah Chapter 32 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 32 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 32 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 32.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 32, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The king of Babylon's army besieged Jerusalem
Jeremiah was shut up in the court of the prison
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Jeremiah 32:1.

questions.question: Who was shut up in the court of the prison?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was shut up in the court of the prison as per Jeremiah 32:2.

questions.question: What did Zedekiah say to Jeremiah regarding his prophecies?
options: You will be taken to Babylon
You will be given a field
questions.correctAnswer: Wherefore dost thou prophesy?
questions.explanation: This question is directly from Zedekiah’s words to Jeremiah in Jeremiah 32:3.

questions.question: According to the Lord, what will happen to Zedekiah king of Judah?
options: He shall escape from the Chaldeans
He shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon
He will lead the people to victory
He will become a great leader
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: This is explicitly stated in Jeremiah 32:4.

questions.question: What will Zedekiah do in Babylon according to the Lord?
options: He shall speak with the king mouth to mouth
questions.correctAnswer: He shall speak with the king mouth to mouth
questions.explanation: The verse Jeremiah 32:4 mentions that Zedekiah will speak with the king mouth to mouth.

questions.question: What is the price Jeremiah paid for the field?
questions.correctAnswer: Seventeen shekels of silver
questions.explanation: Jeremiah bought the field for seventeen shekels of silver as stated in Jeremiah 32:9.

questions.question: Who did Jeremiah give the evidence of the purchase to?
questions.correctAnswer: Baruch
questions.explanation: Jeremiah gave the evidence of the purchase to Baruch as stated in Jeremiah 32:12.

questions.question: What did the Lord instruct Jeremiah to do with the evidence of the purchase?
options: Put it in an earthen vessel
questions.correctAnswer: Put it in an earthen vessel
questions.explanation: The Lord commanded Jeremiah to put the evidence in an earthen vessel as stated in Jeremiah 32:14.

questions.question: What shall be possessed again in the land according to the Lord?
questions.correctAnswer: Houses and fields and vineyards
questions.explanation: This is stated in Jeremiah 32:15, expressing God's promise for the future.

questions.question: What was the condition of Jeremiah when he received the word of the Lord?
options: He was in the court of the prison
questions.correctAnswer: He was in the court of the prison
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was shut up in the court of the prison according to Jeremiah 32:2.

questions.question: Was Hanameel the son of Shallum related to Jeremiah?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, he was his uncle
questions.explanation: Hanameel is identified as the son of Shallum, Jeremiah's uncle, in Jeremiah 32:7.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Babylon's army besieged Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This fact is stated in Jeremiah 32:2.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was allowed to speak freely in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was shut up in the court of the prison, indicating he was not free to speak freely, as mentioned in Jeremiah 32:2.

questions.question: True or False: Zedekiah will escape the hand of the Chaldeans.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:4 states that Zedekiah shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah bought a field from his cousin.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah bought the field from Hanameel, who is his uncle's son, not his cousin, as stated in Jeremiah 32:8.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 32 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 32 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah do after delivering the evidence of the purchase to Baruch?
questions.correctAnswer: He prayed unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah prayed after delivering the evidence of the purchase, as stated in Jeremiah 32:16.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 32:17 promise will happen if someone acknowledges God's power?
options: Nothing is too hard for God
They will be blessed with wealth
They will be led to victory
questions.correctAnswer: Nothing is too hard for God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah acknowledges God's creative power and asserts that nothing is too hard for Him in Jeremiah 32:17.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah say about God's character in Jeremiah 32:18?
options: He shows kindness only to the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: He is loving and just
questions.explanation: Jeremiah describes God as showing lovingkindness and recompensing iniquity, highlighting His justice and mercy in Jeremiah 32:18.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 32:19, what does God observe about the actions of men?
options: He is unaware of their doings
His eyes are open upon all their ways
questions.correctAnswer: His eyes are open upon all their ways
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:19 states that God's eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men, indicating His awareness of their actions.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 32:23 indicate about Israel's response to God's commands?
questions.correctAnswer: They disobeyed His commands
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:23 reveals that the people of Israel did not obey God's voice or walk in His law, leading to their punishment.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 32:24 highlight about the siege of the city?
options: It was foretold by the prophets
It was an act of God’s mercy
It was caused by hunger and pestilence
questions.correctAnswer: It was foretold by the prophets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:24 states that what God had spoken is coming to pass, showing that the siege was foretold.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 32:26, what does God ask Jeremiah regarding His power?
options: Is anything too hard for me?
Am I not the God of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Is anything too hard for me?
questions.explanation: God directly asks Jeremiah if there is anything too hard for Him in Jeremiah 32:27, emphasizing His omnipotence.

questions.question: What future event does Jeremiah 32:28 predict for the city?
options: It will be given to the Chaldeans
questions.correctAnswer: It will be given to the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:28 states that the city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, highlighting the impending judgement.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 32:30, what has Israel done since their youth?
questions.correctAnswer: Provoked God to anger
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:30 indicates that Israel has only done evil and provoked God to anger throughout their history.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 32:15 say about the future of houses and fields in the land?
options: They will be given to the Chaldeans
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be possessed again
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:15 promises that houses, fields, and vineyards will be possessed again in the land, indicating hope for restoration.

questions.question: The events in Jeremiah 32 demonstrate the necessity of which of the following?
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commands
questions.explanation: The chapter emphasizes the consequences of disobedience and the importance of following God's commands.

questions.question: Jeremiah's purchase of the field represents what principle in faith?
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God's promises
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's act of buying the field despite the circumstances shows faith in God's promise of restoration.

questions.question: True or False: God expresses regret for Israel's actions in Jeremiah 32.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: There is no expression of regret from God; rather, He states the consequences of Israel's continuous wrongdoing.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was imprisoned when he received God's word.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was indeed imprisoned when he received the word of the LORD, as stated in Jeremiah 32:2.

questions.question: True or False: God promised that the Chaldeans would be defeated in Jeremiah 32.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: God actually foretells that the Chaldeans will take the city, indicating that they will not be defeated in this context.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 32 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 32.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 32:31, how has the city been described in relation to God's feelings since its construction?
options: A provocation of mine anger and of my fury
A source of joy and blessing
A place of peace and safety
A symbol of hope and redemption
questions.correctAnswer: A provocation of mine anger and of my fury
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:31 states, 'For this city hath been to me as a provocation of mine anger and of my fury from the day that they built it even unto this day; that I should remove it from before my face,' explicitly describing the city's effect on God's anger and fury.

questions.question: Who are included in the groups that provoked God's anger according to Jeremiah 32:32?
options: Kings, princes, priests, prophets, men of Judah, and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Kings, princes, priests, prophets, men of Judah, and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:32 lists these specific groups as those who 'have done to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.'

questions.question: What did the people do to God according to Jeremiah 32:33, despite His early and persistent teaching?
options: They turned unto me the back, and not the face
They built altars and worshiped God faithfully
questions.correctAnswer: They turned unto me the back, and not the face
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:33 states, 'And they have turned unto me the back, and not the face: though I taught them, rising up early and teaching them, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction,' indicating their deliberate turning away.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 32:35, what abominable practice did the people perform in the valley of the son of Hinnom?
options: Causing their sons and daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech
Offering sacrifices to the LORD in the temple
Building altars to the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Causing their sons and daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:35 states, 'And they built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should do this abomination.'

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do in Jeremiah 32:37 about the people driven into captivity?
options: Gather them out of all countries and bring them again unto this place
Forget them and allow their captivity to continue forever
Send another nation to conquer them
questions.correctAnswer: Gather them out of all countries and bring them again unto this place
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:37 declares, 'Behold, I will gather them out of all countries, whither I have driven them in mine anger, and in my fury, and in great wrath; and I will bring them again unto this place,' promising restoration.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 32:44, where are the fields that men shall buy located?
options: In the land of Benjamin, places about Jerusalem, cities of Judah, mountains, valley, and south
Only in the city of Jerusalem
In foreign lands across the seas
In the wilderness outside the Promised Land
questions.correctAnswer: In the land of Benjamin, places about Jerusalem, cities of Judah, mountains, valley, and south
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:44 lists these exact areas: 'in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the valley, and in the cities of the south,' where fields shall be bought.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'חֶרֶם' (cherem) in Jeremiah 32:35 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Devoted to destruction
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'חֶרֶם' (cherem) commonly means 'devoted to destruction' or under a ban, fitting the context of abominable practices in Jeremiah 32:35.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Jeremiah 32:39-40, where God promises one heart and one way to fear Him forever?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:39-40 uses a chiastic structure emphasizing God's covenant and the unity of heart and way, a common Hebrew literary device to highlight central theology.

questions.question: Which Bible passage echoes the theme of God's everlasting covenant and restoration found in Jeremiah 32:40?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel 36:26-27
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:26-27 parallels Jeremiah 32:40 with God's promise to give a new heart and spirit, underscoring covenantal restoration.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the promise of God giving one heart and one way to fear Him as stated in Jeremiah 32:39?
questions.explanation: John 14:16-17 describes the coming of the Holy Spirit who dwells with believers, uniting their hearts and ways to God, fulfilling Jeremiah 32:39.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the promise in Jeremiah 32:37 that God will gather His people from all countries?
options: A declaration of the city’s coming destruction by Babylon
The purchase of a field by Jeremiah
A lament over the exile of Israel
A vision of the new temple
questions.correctAnswer: A declaration of the city’s coming destruction by Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:36 speaks of the city being delivered to Babylon by sword, famine, and pestilence, immediately preceding the gathering promise in 32:37.

questions.question: In the context of Jeremiah 32, what is the significance of Jeremiah buying a field in Anathoth?
options: It symbolizes hope for restoration and future possession of the land
It was a political act to support the Babylonian king
It was a bribe to gain favor with the priests
It represented Jeremiah's surrender to exile
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes hope for restoration and future possession of the land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:9-15 details the purchase as a prophetic act signifying God's promise of restoration despite current captivity.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Jeremiah 32:42 where God's promise of good is balanced against the evil brought upon the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:42 uses parallelism by contrasting the evil brought upon the people with the good God promises to bring, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 32:27 emphasize God's omnipotence?
options: By asking rhetorically if anything is too hard for the LORD
By listing all the miracles God has done
By recounting the creation story in detail
By describing God's anger against the people
questions.correctAnswer: By asking rhetorically if anything is too hard for the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:27 says, 'Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?' emphasizing God's unlimited power.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 32:34, the people set their abominations in the house called by God's name to defile it.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:34 explicitly states, 'But they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it,' confirming this statement.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 32 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 32 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 32:27 teach about God's nature?
options: God is omnipotent and nothing is too hard for Him
God is limited by human actions
God is indifferent to human sin
God is bound by covenant only to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God is omnipotent and nothing is too hard for Him
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:27 states, 'Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?' affirming God's omnipotence.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment and mercy does Jeremiah 32:37 teach?
options: God will gather and restore His people after judgment
God will permanently exile His people without hope
God's judgment is arbitrary and unchangeable
God only judges individuals, not nations
questions.correctAnswer: God will gather and restore His people after judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:37 says, 'Behold, I will gather them out of all countries... and I will bring them again unto this place,' showing God's mercy in restoration after judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sinfulness is taught in Jeremiah 32:30?
options: Human sin is persistent and provokes God's anger from youth
Human sin is easily forgiven without repentance
Human sin affects only personal relationships, not covenant
Human sin is excused by God due to election
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin is persistent and provokes God's anger from youth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:30 states, 'For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have only done evil before me from their youth,' highlighting persistent sin provoking divine anger.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 32:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Lovingkindness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:18 praises God who 'shewest lovingkindness unto thousands,' emphasizing His steadfast love and mercy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Jeremiah 32:40?
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:40 states, 'And I will make an everlasting covenant with them,' demonstrating God's steadfast covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 32:15 connect to the broader biblical theme of land restoration in Scripture?
options: It anticipates the eschatological promise of renewed possession of the Promised Land
It denies any future restoration for Israel
It focuses solely on immediate exile without hope
It teaches that land possession is irrelevant to covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the eschatological promise of renewed possession of the Promised Land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:15 declares 'Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again,' linking to the biblical theme of restoration seen in books like Ezekiel and Isaiah.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Jeremiah 32:21 make regarding God's acts of salvation?
options: It recalls the Exodus as a foundational act of God's salvation history
It denies any historical acts of God's salvation
It equates salvation only with future promises without past acts
It claims salvation comes through human effort
questions.correctAnswer: It recalls the Exodus as a foundational act of God's salvation history
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:21 references God bringing 'forth thy people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders,' connecting current promises to the Exodus narrative.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 32:40 and 32:38 teach about God's covenant and His people?
options: God establishes an everlasting covenant resulting in a faithful relationship with His people
God rejects any covenant with His people
God's covenant is conditional on human perfection
God's covenant excludes the promise of internal transformation
questions.correctAnswer: God establishes an everlasting covenant resulting in a faithful relationship with His people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:40 and 32:38 together affirm that God will make an everlasting covenant and that 'they shall be my people, and I will be their God,' signifying a faithful relational bond.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 32:33 and 32:34 teach about human response to divine teaching and holiness of the temple?
options: Human rebellion includes rejecting God's instruction and defiling His holy place
Humans universally obey God's instruction and keep the temple pure
Defilement of the temple is justified by cultural practices
God condones turning away from His teachings
questions.correctAnswer: Human rebellion includes rejecting God's instruction and defiling His holy place
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:33 notes they 'have not hearkened,' and 32:34 describes defiling 'the house... called by my name,' indicating rejection of God’s instruction and temple holiness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 32:26 and 32:28 teach about God's sovereignty and judgment on Jerusalem?
options: God sovereignly declares the city will fall to Babylon as part of His judgment
God is powerless to prevent the city's fall
God will protect Jerusalem from Babylon unconditionally
God's judgment is based on random chance
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly declares the city will fall to Babylon as part of His judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:26-28 show God speaking through Jeremiah to declare the city's fall to Babylon as an act of divine sovereignty and judgment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 32:43-44 offers false hope because the land is desolate and will never be repurchased. What does Jeremiah 32:43-44 actually teach?
options: Fields will be bought again, evidencing a future restoration and return from captivity
The land will remain desolate forever without human settlement
God has abandoned His promises to Israel regarding the land
The purchase of land is a symbolic act with no real future significance
questions.correctAnswer: Fields will be bought again, evidencing a future restoration and return from captivity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:43-44 states that men shall buy fields and take witnesses to the purchase, signifying real, future restoration despite current desolation.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and recompense is taught in Jeremiah 32:19?
options: God gives every one according to their ways and the fruit of their doings
God ignores human actions and acts arbitrarily
God rewards all people equally regardless of behavior
God's justice is limited to the present life only
questions.correctAnswer: God gives every one according to their ways and the fruit of their doings
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:19 explains that God’s eyes are open to all ways and He rewards each according to their deeds, emphasizing divine justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Jeremiah 32:41?
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful commitment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:41 states, 'Yea, I will rejoice over them to do them good,' highlighting God's joyful commitment to blessing His people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about sin and covenant renewal is taught in Jeremiah 32:35 and 32:39?
options: Sin provokes judgment, but God promises a transformed heart leading to covenant faithfulness
Sin has no consequences on covenant relationship
God's covenant is unconditional regardless of heart transformation
questions.correctAnswer: Sin provokes judgment, but God promises a transformed heart leading to covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:35 describes abominable sin causing judgment, while 32:39 promises God will give 'one heart, and one way' so they fear Him forever, indicating heart transformation and renewed covenant.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 32:7-11 illustrate theological truths about covenant rights and hope amidst judgment?
options: The purchase of land demonstrates hope and covenant rights even during siege and exile
Property rights are irrelevant during divine judgment
Hope is misplaced if the city is destined for destruction
Covenant rights are nullified by military defeat
questions.correctAnswer: The purchase of land demonstrates hope and covenant rights even during siege and exile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 32:7-11 shows Jeremiah buying land during the siege, symbolizing hope and the enduring nature of covenant promises despite judgment.
